answer: One retina, one agent: a certified centre scans the blood-vessel pattern inside the operator's eye, hashes the template, and signs a fresh challenge binding that hash to the agent's key, re-checked every epoch. A second key claiming the same retina is rejected outright, since the centre, not the claimant, holds the record. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 supervised scans at about $40 each, roughly $40,000 — like light through a prism, one retina yields a single template; no attacker can wander between identities on the same eye, and no raven can lend its eye to a second agent.
